bargain = something sold at a very good, low price
discount = an amount taken off the usual price
sale = a time when a shop sells things cheaper than usual
receipt = a piece of paper that proves you paid
refund = money you get back when you return goods
exchange = to give something back and get another size or item
cash desk = the place in a shop where you pay
credit card = a plastic card you use to pay and pay the bank later
cash = money in notes and coins, not a card
try on = to put on clothes in a shop to check the size
fit = to be the right size for your body
size = how big or small a piece of clothing is
window shopping = looking at shop windows without buying
shopping centre = a building with many shops together
department store = a large shop that sells many kinds of goods
grocer's = a shop that sells food such as fruit, tins and rice
butcher's = a shop that sells meat
baker's = a shop that sells bread and cakes
newsagent's = a shop that sells newspapers, magazines and sweets
queue = a line of people waiting
customer = a person who buys something in a shop
brand = the name of a company that makes a product
second-hand = already used by someone else; not new
online shopping = buying goods on the internet
delivery = bringing goods to your home
expensive = costing a lot of money
cheap = costing little money
value for money = good quality for the price you pay
hairdresser's = a shop where you have your hair cut
post office = a place where you send letters and parcels
bank account = an arrangement with a bank to keep your money
withdraw = to take money out of a bank account
ATM = a machine that gives you cash from your account
afford = to have enough money to buy something
price = how much you must pay for something
open late = staying open after the usual closing time
shop = a place where you buy things
store = a large shop
supermarket = a large shop that sells food and household goods
hypermarket = a very large supermarket, often with parking
corner shop = a small local shop, often open late
market stall = a table outdoors where a person sells goods
flea market = a market for old or second-hand things
mall = a large indoor shopping centre
high street = the main street in a town with shops
outlet = a shop that sells last season's goods cheaper
bookshop = a shop that sells books
clothes shop = a shop that sells clothes
shoe shop = a shop that sells shoes
sports shop = a shop that sells sports clothes and equipment
toy shop = a shop that sells toys
chemist's = a shop that sells medicine and toiletries
optician's = a shop that tests eyes and sells glasses
jeweller's = a shop that sells watches and jewellery
dry cleaner's = a shop that cleans clothes you cannot wash at home
shoe repair = a service that mends shoes
travel agent's = a shop that books holidays
estate agent's = a shop that sells or rents houses
petrol station shop = a small shop at a place where cars buy fuel
vending machine = a machine that sells drinks or snacks after you put money in
checkout = the place in a supermarket where you pay
self-service till = a machine where you scan and pay yourself
shopping basket = a small container you carry while you shop
trolley = a large basket on wheels in a supermarket
carrier bag = a bag from a shop, often plastic or paper
loyalty card = a shop card that gives points or discounts
gift card = a card with money on it to spend in a shop
voucher = a ticket that gives you money off or a free item
special offer = a lower price for a short time
two for one = a deal where you get two items but pay for one
half price = costing 50 percent less than usual
reduced = sold for less because it will expire or is last season
best before = the date after which food may not taste as good
use by = the last date you should eat a product for safety
bar code = the pattern of lines a scanner reads on a product
label = the paper on a product with name, price or size
price tag = a small label showing how much something costs
till receipt = the printed proof of payment from the till
PIN = the secret number you type when you pay by card
contactless = paying by tapping a card or phone, without a PIN
debit card = a card that takes money straight from your bank account
notes = paper money
coins = metal money
change = money you get back when you pay with too much
keep the change = to let the seller keep extra money as a tip
overcharge = to ask for more money than the correct price
undercharge = to ask for less money than the correct price
complaint = a statement that something is wrong with goods or service
complain = to say you are not satisfied
manager = the person in charge of a shop
customer service desk = the place in a shop for returns and questions
return = to take goods back to the shop
guarantee = a promise to repair or replace a product if it breaks
warranty = a written promise that a product will work for a period
faulty = not working correctly
out of stock = not in the shop at the moment
in stock = available to buy now
sold out = with no items left to sell
order = a request to buy goods; to make that request
click and collect = buying on the internet and picking up in a shop
home delivery = when a shop brings goods to your house
track a parcel = to follow where a package is on its way to you
courier = a person or company that delivers parcels
postage = the money you pay to send a letter or parcel
stamp = a small paper you stick on a letter to pay for sending it
parcel = something wrapped to send in the post
open an account = to start a bank account
savings = money you keep for later
lend = to give money that must be given back
borrow money = to take money that you must pay back
owe = to need to pay money back to someone
be broke = to have no money (informal)
save up = to keep money until you have enough to buy something
splash out = to spend a lot of money on something you want
good deal = a purchase at a fair or low price
rip-off = something that costs far too much (informal)
shop around = to compare prices in different shops before you buy
browse = to look at goods without a plan to buy at once
queue-jump = to go in front of people who were waiting first
opening hours = the times when a shop is open
closed = not open for customers
open 24 hours = open all day and all night
fitting room = a small room in a clothes shop for trying clothes on
